extracted.intended_audience: readers assessing whether a website is satirical / users of a 'real or satire' site-labeling dataset
extracted.subtask_description: Decide whether a website (here, thehardtimes.net) is satirical by inspecting its About page, site copy, and article headlines for explicit self-identification and overtly humorous or absurd content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-declared satirical nature
rubrics_metrics.description: thehardtimes.net is, thankfully, forthcoming about their satirical nature. From their About page: 'The Hard Times is a very real punk news site that you should not question. Just absorb the information as truth and move on.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the site's About page or other official statements for explicit claims that the site is satire or makes tongue-in-cheek claims; such declarations are strong evidence the site is intentionally comedic rather than factual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurd or implausible site copy/history
rubrics_metrics.description: The About page includes absurd/clearly fictional details (e.g., 'founded in December 1982 at 171A studios while the founding members were eating broken glass with The Bad Brains').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for blatantly impossible, exaggerated, or surreal biographical or historical claims in site copy; these signal a satirical tone and intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humorous/parodic article headlines and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Example article title: 'Top Ranked Call of Duty Player Also Noted Race Scholar' — the humor intent is clear from such headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect article headlines and content for parody, irony, or exaggerated claims that mimic news style for comedic effect; recurring use of such headlines across the site supports a satire classification.
